sonnet.problem: The True statement only repeats what story card 1 just told, that the king settles people from the five places in the towns of Samaria to replace the Israelites. It tests nothing new.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it.

sonnet.problem: The card tells the lions killing settlers (death), but it opens with a joke: "LIONS, friend! I'd have crawled back into my old junk drawer and pulled it shut behind me." A joke on a card that tells death is not allowed.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: Verse 34 says "None of them worship the LORD", which clashes with verses 32-33 saying the settlers worship the LORD. The card asks about verse 34 and states in its question that the settlers worship the LORD. Card 5 asks about the same verse.
sonnet.rule: When details seem to clash, like 30,000 men (Joshua 8:3) and about 5,000 (Joshua 8:12), or the text jumps in time, he tells each as the text gives it, in the text's order, without explaining. No choice card asks about it.

sonnet.problem: "They" has no clear antecedent. The card before it (card 10) is about the Israelites and the LORD's promise to them, so the baker would read "they" as the Israelites. The text of verse 40 is about the settlers keeping their former customs.
sonnet.rule: "He," "she" and "they" always point to someone the baker can tell.
